water.name: Land
water.rule: At least half of the hex’s sample points (one every 4 km) fall on land (GISCO country outlines), outside Natural Earth lakes.

water.name: Ocean
water.rule: Sea deeper than 200 m and not next to land.

water.name: Coast
water.rule: Sea next to a land hex, or shallower than 200 m (mean of the Terrarium/SRTM samples).

water.name: Lake
water.rule: Water hex where Natural Earth 1:10m lake samples outnumber sea samples.

relief.name: Flat
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation inside the hex under 85 m.

relief.name: Mountains
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation ≥ 260 m, or mean elevation ≥ 2,000 m.

relief.name: Peaks
relief.rule: Mean elevation ≥ 2,300 m, or a summit ≥ 3,500 m with a standard deviation ≥ 400 m (alpine).

cover.name: None
cover.rule: Water, land outside the map’s countries, or no WorldCover samples.

cover.name: Deciduous forest
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Tree cover (10), drawn as broadleaf below 52°N and 500 m is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Conifer forest
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Tree cover (10), drawn as conifer above 58°N or 900 m is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Mixed forest
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Tree cover (10), drawn as mixed forest in between is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Scrub & desert
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Shrubland (20) plus moss & lichen (100) is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Grassland
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Grassland (30) at or above 600 m (alpine meadows, rough grazing) is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Pasture
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Grassland (30) below 600 m (mostly managed pasture and meadows) is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Cropland
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Cropland (40) is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Wetland
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Herbaceous wetland (90) and mangroves (95) is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Urban
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Built-up (50) ≥ 22% of the hex’s land samples

cover.name: Barren
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Bare / sparse vegetation (60) is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

cover.name: Ice & snow
cover.rule: ESA WorldCover 2021 class Snow and ice (70) is the largest group of the hex’s land samples.

notes.water: Census 1:20M state outlines and Natural Earth 1:50m country and lake outlines don't meet exactly. A sea hex whose ETOPO1 mean is above sea level (and under half of its samples below it) becomes land when at least 4 of its 6 neighbours are land, or when it touches both US and foreign land; it takes the neighbours' majority owner. Narrow reservoirs that cover less than half a hex are land, and their river is drawn through them. Tidal bays stay water when the hex centre is sea and its ETOPO1 mean is at or below sea level or at least half of its ETOPO1 samples are. A sea hex's elevation is the mean of its ETOPO1 samples below sea level (its water depth).
notes.relief: From ETOPO1 samples (~9 km apart, about 20 per hex) with altitude ≥ -100 m, so bays and sea floor don't count; all samples are used if none qualify. Water hexes are always flat.
notes.cover: From NLCD 2021 (~2 km pixels), sampled on a 2 km lattice inside each US hex (about 400 points). Open water (11) and no-data pixels are ignored; shares are of the remaining land points, rounded to whole percent, and the urban threshold is applied to the rounded developed share. NLCD covers only the lower 48, so foreign hexes (Canada, Mexico, the Caribbean) have cover 0 (none).
